question: Does observing capacity before quality and controlling final normal work change the service feasibility conclusion?
assumptions:
Round70: does controlled normal work overcome the fixed-forward service limit?

An optional broader policy class, not a change to the frozen canonical model.
Only allow final normal work x to be selected after capacity is known but before
ANY initial quality or repair outcomes are observed. Earlier stations stay
greedy. Aggregate workloads only; no job-level schedule or profit claim.
For service, larger I expands x's feasible set, so I2100 covers all smaller
integer releases and larger ones have identical flows. iid/DM quality laws and
repair success probabilities stay unchanged. No setup workload, single route.
finite_control_argument:
Service-only normal/rework allocation at the final station, before quality.

Given known integer capacity C and normal-flow upper bound U, choose x<=U.
N=floor(y*x), L=floor(C-x), with setup workload0. Conditional service is
nondecreasing in N for fixed L (consistent iid/DM item sequences, same repair
law). A fractional x is weakly dominated for SERVICE by ceil(x) if feasible,
else U: it has the same L and at least as many initial items. Hence integers
plus U suffice for exact continuous-x service maximization in this model.
This does not establish profit optimality or physical scheduling feasibility.
